title: Deformation of solids

parts.text:
20 A sample of material is stretched by a tensile force to a point beyond its elastic limit. The tensile
force is then reduced to zero. The force–extension graph is shown.
force
Y
X
Z
extension
0
0
Which area represents the net work done on the sample?
A
X
B
X + Y
C
Y + Z
D
Z

hints: Notice the arrows on the force-extension graph and the permanent extension where the unloading line meets the extension axis.
Recall that work done in stretching is the area under the force against extension curve, so loading and unloading give different areas.
Compare the large area under the upper loading curve with the smaller area $Z$ under the lower unloading line to find work in minus work out.
walkthrough: Identify the loading curve with the upward arrows from zero extension to maximum extension. The work done on the sample during stretching is the area under this curve, which is $X+Y+Z$.
Identify the unloading curve with the downward arrow back to zero force. The sample does work as it contracts, and this recovered work is the area under the unloading line, which is $Z$.
Find the net work done on the sample as work in minus work recovered: $(X+Y+Z) - Z = X+Y$.
This net area is the hysteresis loop trapped between the loading and unloading lines, and it represents energy dissipated as heat and permanent plastic deformation. This is option B.

A.explanation: Area $X$ is only the small triangle under the initial elastic part of the loading curve, not the total work put in during stretching.

B.explanation: Area $X+Y$ is the loading area minus the unloading area, so it is the hysteresis loop and the net work retained as plastic deformation and heat.

C.explanation: Area $Y+Z$ omits $X$ and includes $Z$, so it does not equal work in minus work recovered.

D.explanation: Area $Z$ under the unloading line is the elastic strain energy recovered when the force is removed, not the net work done.
